newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua coffee crop seen falling short of hopes.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua coffee crop seen falling short of hopes.

text.p: Nicaragua's top coffee grower on Friday said Nicaragua's 1996-7 coffee harvest will fall far short of earlier projections, mainly due to a lack of financing for growers.

The new president of the Nicaraguan Union of Coffee Growers (Unicafe), Amilcar Navarro, said Nicaragua's 1996-97 coffee harvest will likely be about one million quintales (100-lb bags), down from the 1,215,867 quintales Unicafe had projected.
With difficulty "we think we can reach one million quintales," Navarro told reporters.
Navarro replaces outgoing Unicafe President David Robleto, who left to become Minister of Foreign Cooperation in the government of President Arnoldo Aleman, which took power on January 10.
Navarro told reporters Unicafe would release a more complete report on the coffee harvest next week.

He said coffee production was hurt by a suspension of credit to indebted growers, the coffee disease "la roya," and the poor state of the roads in coffee-growing regions, especially because of storm damage from Hurricane Cesar.
Navarro said under ideal conditions, Nicaragua should have harvested 1.6 million quintales in 1996-97.
